title: BIRP note from F1: every section written + planted facts recalled
hypothesis: The BIRP template produces a complete note that captures the session's key facts.

sections.title: Behavior
sections.html:
Client presented for a 50-minute individual CBT session with a diagnosis of F41.0 Panic disorder. Client reported a rough week, noting a panic attack on Tuesday at the grocery store checkout line characterized by pounding heart, resulting in leaving the cart and exiting the store. Client identified automatic thoughts of passing out in front of everyone and being perceived as crazy, rating belief in this thought at 90% in the moment and 40% later at home. Client reported completing two out of three assigned thought records. Sleep was reported as poor, approximately four hours per night with early morning awakening around 3:00 AM. Client reported starting sertraline 50 mg approximately two weeks ago via primary care, with initial mild nausea that has since resolved. Safety check was negative for suicidal ideation or intent; client expressed a desire for panic symptoms to cease. Client mentioned unhelpful support from sister Dana.

Client denied homicidal ideation. Mental status observations were not explicitly detailed beyond participation in session tasks.

sections.title: Intervention
sections.html:
• Reviewed completed thought records and explored cognitive distortions and belief ratings regarding panic triggers.
  • Conducted safety check regarding suicidal ideation and intent.
  • Utilized interoceptive exposure by having the Client spin in a chair for 30 seconds to intentionally elicit dizziness and observe the physiological response.
  • Discussed psychoeducation on the peak-and-decline nature of anxiety sensations without avoidance.
  • Explored potential family involvement in treatment, which the Client declined at this time.

sections.title: Response
sections.html: Client engaged in reviewing the thought records and recognized the shift in belief rating from 90% during the panic attack to 40% at home. Client denied thoughts of self-harm or suicide. During the interoceptive exposure exercise, the Client reported anxiety reaching a 6 out of 10 after spinning, which decreased to a 3 within two minutes. Client acknowledged the therapist's processing that sensations peaked and passed without leaving the environment. Client declined bringing sister Dana to a session at this time, preferring to postpone family involvement.

sections.title: Plan
sections.html:
• Complete thought records three times in the coming week.
  • Practice the interoceptive spinning exercise once a day at home.
  • Attempt a graded in-vivo exposure by returning to the grocery store on a quiet Saturday morning and staying until anxiety levels drop by half.
  • Attend next individual psychotherapy session at the scheduled time next week.
